jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager (Security)
jobs.description:
This role will be based in Mountain View, CA.

At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

About the team:

LinkedIn's members entrust us with their information every day and we take their security seriously. Our core value of putting our members first powers all the decisions we make, including how we manage and protect the data of our members and customers. Information Security at LinkedIn is dedicated to protecting and securing business-critical member data and company assets. Our core mission is to empower LinkedIn to create a secure and thriving platform for every member of the global workforce.

We’re hiring a Staff Security Technical Program Manager to drive execution across our Production and Enterprise Security organization. You’ll own critical programs such as vulnerability management, lead cross-functional security initiatives, and establish the operating rhythm that keeps teams aligned on priorities, OKRs, milestones, and outcomes.

You’ll bring structure to complex programs, surface risks and dependencies early, drive decisions to closure, and ensure commitments don’t fall through the cracks. You’ll provide leadership with clear, accurate program status while serving as a force multiplier for engineers by removing blockers and creating clarity without adding unnecessary process.

About the role:

We are seeking a Security Technical Program Manager to join LinkedIn’s centralized TPM Infra organization. In this critical role, you will build and scale a mature production and enterprise security architecture to protect our global platform, members, and organizational assets. You will serve as a key driver across security governance, operational cadences, metrics telemetry, cross-functional program execution, and executive accountability for production and enterprise risk reduction.

Responsibilities:

• Lead end-to-end security remediation strategy across the products and infra org by consolidating findings from threat models, code reviews, penetration tests, vulnerability assessments, audits, and postmortems into a unified backlog with clear ownership, prioritization, and defined SLAs.
• Establish standardized frameworks for risk identification, tracking, exception management, escalation paths, and remediation validation to ensure operational consistency across security programs.
• Define standardized metrics and telemetry dashboards to deliver actionable risk insights for leadership, enabling proactive tracking of systemic vulnerabilities and cross-team remediation accountability.
• Establish organizational operating rhythms, including goal setting, dependency mapping, key milestone tracking, and quarterly executive readouts, to maintain continuous visibility into OKR execution across security initiatives.
• Manage the vulnerability management lifecycle, including scanning scope, remediation cadences, risk exception workflows, and executive reporting on organizational risk posture.
• Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure third-party security evaluations remain efficient, standardized, and transparent for internal requesters.
• Drive complex security programs from initiation to delivery by orchestrating work across Security, IT, Legal, HR, and Compliance partners while ensuring accountability on deliverables.
• Establish organizational operating rhythms, including sprint planning, OKR tracking, and backlog governance, to maintain continuous visibility into program execution.
• Elevate documentation standards for program specifications, standard operating procedures, architectural decisions, and incident action items to maintain clarity and discoverability.
• Establish metrics and key performance indicators to evaluate program effectiveness and convert security telemetry into actionable technical insights.
• Lead postmortem reviews and remediation governance for major security incidents, converting key takeaways into resilient architectural controls, automated mechanisms, and updated operating procedures.
• Define standardized metrics and telemetry dashboards to deliver actionable risk insights for leadership, enabling proactive tracking of systemic vulnerabilities and cross-team remediation accountability.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, Finance, or a related field.
• 7+ years of experience in technical program management, including a minimum of 3 years leading complex security initiatives.
• Demonstrated track record of orchestrating company-wide vulnerability management lifecycles, driving cross-functional remediation, establishing governance SLAs, and reporting posture metrics to leadership.
• Technical expertise to engage effectively with engineering teams, evaluate security risk factors, and navigate fundamental information protection principles across complex domains.
• Technical depth to engage effectively with security engineers, assess threat severity, evaluate exploitability, and critically review risk determinations.
• Extensive experience managing agile operating rhythms, OKR tracking, task management platforms (such as Jira or Linear), documentation repositories, and executive reporting dashboards.
• Exceptional written communication skills with an emphasis on clarity, brevity, and structured documentation.
• Proven ability to partner effectively across engineering, IT, Legal, HR, and Compliance teams to achieve business alignment and deliver organizational results.
• Collaborative mindset with high emotional intelligence and an inclusive approach to problem-solving across diverse organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

• BS and 8+ years of relevant work experience
• Demonstrated history of partnering with engineering organizations to deliver high-impact, enterprise-scale security initiatives.
• Outstanding written and verbal communication capabilities, with a proven track record of adapting complex messaging for diverse technical and executive audiences.
• Proven ability to influence cross-functional partners and engineering leadership to align priorities and advance key security programs.

Suggested Skills

• Strategic Portfolio Management
• Executive Influence & Stakeholder Leadership
• Enterprise Program Delivery
• Operating Model & Governance
• Executive Communication & Risk Management
• Comprehensive understanding of fundamental information security paradigms and security architecture principles

jobs.title: Director, Payloads Systems Integration and Test
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About this role

As Director of Payload Systems Integration and Test, you will lead and grow a team of multidisciplinary engineers responsible for end-to-end mission success of a diverse portfolio of payloads, such as inertial, RF, and optical sensors and communication systems, as well as various types of pharmaceutical processing payloads. This role combines deep technical authority with team leadership, product definition, and customer delivery
responsibility. You will own the successful execution of multiple concurrent payload missions, delivering flight hardware that operates in orbit, survives hypersonic reentry, and returns to Earth – reliably and at scale.

Your team will serve as the technical bridge between each payload and the Varda vehicle, defining interfaces, planning and executing payload integration and test campaigns, coordinating in-orbit operations, and ensuring safe recovery of payload data and hardware. When payloads require special accommodations or vehicle modifications, your team will work across the vehicle engineering team to scope and implement these changes.

As Director, you will manage day-to-day execution across the team, in addition to hiring and headcount planning, new project scoping, and development of standard workflows and processes. You will also own and evolve the Varda Payload User Guide, defining standard interfaces and accommodations for hosted payloads, and developing a roadmap that expands the set of customers and use cases Varda can support while simultaneously growing mission cadence.

Responsibilities

• Build and lead the Payload Systems Integration & Test team, hiring and developing engineers across a range of experience levels

• Own integration and test for Varda's internal pharmaceutical processing payloads: test planning, functional and process verification, contamination control, and environmental qualification of fluidic and thermal flight hardware

• Partner closely with Payload & Mechanisms development engineers on pharma payload designs, staying engaged early enough in the design cycle to shape testability, and supporting the fast iteration these programs run on

• Take ambiguous customer mission objectives and determine how to meet them with the existing platform, or scope the non-recurring engineering needed and bring in the right development teams

• Own payload interface definition and requirements: ICDs, interface verification, and the standards documentation (payload user guide) that external customers and internal teams work from

jobs.title: Director, Publications & Medical Information
jobs.description:
About Us

Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.

It is Kardigan’s mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan’s co-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020.

We have a cutting-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late-stage candidates, and an industry-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

At Kardigan, we are motivated by our values which guide how we work, interact, and achieve our goals. Driven by patients and their families, we are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients and prioritizing their needs above all else. We believe in being authentic—leading with truth to bring out the best in others by creating an environment where every person knows they will be fully accepted. With an eagerness to learn, we encourage the highest levels of curiosity and are open to changing our minds. We are committed to winning as a team with urgency, excellence, and intention, and support each other no matter what role we play or where we sit. Lastly, we strive to enable the impossible because patients are counting on us. We are not afraid to take risks to unlock innovation and advance scientific discoveries.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day.

At Kardigan, Medical Affairs serves as the scientific bridge between Research & Development, the external medical community, and future commercial stakeholders. Through evidence generation, scientific communications, and external engagement, we help translate science into meaningful impact for patients and healthcare professionals.

Position Summary

The Director, Publications & Medical Information is a strategic leadership role within Scientific Communications and Medical Affairs responsible for developing and executing integrated evidence dissemination strategies across Kardigan's cardiovascular portfolio.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Scientific Communications, this individual will lead publication strategy, publication governance, scientific narrative execution, medical information operations, and scientific content development to ensure that Kardigan's evidence is communicated effectively, consistently, and compliantly.

The successful candidate will help shape how scientific evidence generated across clinical development, translational research, medical affairs, real-world evidence, and health outcomes research is transformed into impactful publications, congress presentations, medical education, scientific exchange, and medical information resources.

Key Responsibilities

Publications Strategy & Planning

• Co-lead development and execution of integrated publication strategies across all disease areas and development programs.

• Drive alignment between publication plans and broader scientific communication objectives.

• Manage publication agencies and external publication partners.

• Support publication charters and strategic publication plans that align with clinical development milestones, evidence generation strategies, and Medical Affairs objectives.

• Identify publication opportunities across clinical, translational, biomarker, real-world evidence, implementation science, and disease-state education initiatives.

Publication Development & Governance

• Oversee publication development from concept through submission and dissemination.

• Partner with clinical development, biostatistics, regulatory affairs, safety, legal, and research teams throughout publication development.

• Lead publication operations infrastructure including future publication tracking systems, publication dashboards, annual planning processes, publication metrics, budget tracking, and governance workflows.

• Ensure adherence to ICMJE guidelines, GPP standards, authorship policies, Sunshine requirements, and publication-related compliance standards.

• Establish inspection-ready documentation, SOPs, work instructions, and quality management processes supporting publication and medical information activities.

Scientific Narrative & Data Communications

• Partner with Medical Directors and Scientific Communications leadership to develop and maintain scientific narratives and communication platforms across disease states.

• Ensure consistent scientific messaging across publications, congress activities, medical education materials, field medical resources, corporate communications, and investor communications.

Scientific Communications Operations & Excellence

• Lead operational planning, governance, budget management, vendor oversight, and performance reporting across Scientific Communications activities.

• Develop and maintain dashboards and KPIs to measure publication execution, medical information performance, scientific content utilization, and dissemination effectiveness.

• Establish scalable systems, processes, and technologies to support publication management, medical information operations, knowledge management, and launch readiness.

• Identify opportunities to leverage AI and digital solutions to improve efficiency, content development, and insight generation.

Medical Information Leadership

• Build and operationalize Kardigan's Medical Information capabilities as the company advances toward commercialization.

• Lead development and maintenance of:

• Standard Medical Information response documents

• Scientific response letters

• Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

• Medical Information content repositories

• Scientific exchange materials

• Establish and continuously improve inquiry intake, triage, escalation, and response processes.

• Ensure compliance with pharmacovigilance reporting requirements and adverse event identification procedures.

• Analyze inquiry trends and generate insights that inform Medical Strategy, Evidence Generation, and Medical Education priorities.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Serve as a strategic thought partner to Medical Affairs leadership.

• Collaborate extensively with Clinical Development, Research, Regulatory Affairs, Field Medical, Patient Advocacy, Commercial Strategy, and External Affairs.

• Contribute to integrated Medical Strategy Planning and evidence dissemination planning.

Qualifications

Required

• PhD, PharmD or equivalent advanced scientific degree.

• Demonstrated leadership in publications strategy and execution.

• Significant experience managing publication agencies and external vendors.

• Strong understanding of publication guidelines, publication ethics, and scientific communications best practices.

• Experience leading cross-functional teams in complex development-stage environments.

• Exceptional scientific writing, communication, and presentation skills.

Preferred

• 10+ years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or medical communications experience preferred

• Cardiovascular disease experience

• Experience supporting launch or pre-launch products

• Medical Information leadership experience

• CMPP certification

Exact Compensation may vary based on skills, experience and location.

Pay range

$200,000—$275,000 USD

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

ABOUT LITTLE TOKYO BUSINESS ASSOCIATION

The Little Tokyo Business Association (LTBA) is a 501(c)(4) non-profit social welfare organization dedicated to the growth and development of Little Tokyo as a vibrant, diverse, and multi-faceted district of Downtown Los Angeles.

Little Tokyo is a 142-year-old community consisting of approximately 400 mostly small businesses and is the largest of America’s three remaining historic Japantowns. With two world-class museums, two theatres offering live performances, 100 restaurants ranging from Michelin-rated fine dining to snack shops, and the largest concentration of anime and manga stores outside of Japan, Little Tokyo has become one of the most dynamic districts in Downtown Los Angeles.

The district’s ability to resurge after the pandemic and beyond earned Little Tokyo the L.A. Downtown News “Best Business Improvement District” and “Best Shopping” designations five years in a row, from 2020 to 2025.

LTBA has been responsible for managing the Little Tokyo Business Improvement District (LTBID) for over 21 years. In January 2026, the current merchant-based Business Improvement District (BID) converted to a property-based BID, consistent with many other districts in the City of Los Angeles. With a new budget of approximately $1.5 million, LTBA (a volunteer-run organization) will hire staff to oversee LTBID initiatives focusing on Little Tokyo’s cleanliness, safety, and overall positive urban experience.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Executive Director is an exempt, at-will position and will serve as the senior executive leader of LTBID, reporting directly to the LTBA Board President/Senior Vice President and working closely with the BID Advisory Committee, Board of Directors, business and property owners, community partners, and City stakeholders. The Executive Director will lead LTBID operations, including budget and contract oversight, personnel administration, strategic business planning and execution, marketing and communications, and compliance with City of Los Angeles BID guidelines.

The ideal candidate is a community-minded, hands-on leader who combines strategic vision with strong operational and people-management experience. Demonstrated experience working with and supporting a business community is essential, along with the ability to build consensus among diverse stakeholders, manage staff and vendors, and translate priorities into measurable results. The successful candidate will bring strong business acumen and the ability to strengthen Little Tokyo’s economic vitality through marketing, communications, events, public-space activation, and partnerships that elevate the district’s approximately 400 businesses and help attract new businesses and visitors.

Familiarity with Little Tokyo, its history, culture, and community is highly valued. Experience navigating City of Los Angeles rules, ordinances, and processes, particularly those involving Business Improvement Districts and the Office of the City Clerk, is also preferred. The Executive Director should appreciate Little Tokyo’s unique character and identity while helping the community build toward a vibrant, safe, clean, and economically strong future.

ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Leadership and Strategy

• Adhere to business improvement district operating requirements, in conjunction with LTBID’s goals and objectives

• Develop and implement a strategic business plan to ensure LTBID requirements are properly managed, with key performance indicators

• Implement economic vitality and marketing goals to promote Little Tokyo business through economic and business development, creative events, and activation of public spaces.

• Responsible for full range of administrative duties, including but not limited to budget, contract, marketing, and personnel administration.

• Partner with the Board and Board President to support effective governance, decision-making, and implementation of Board priorities.

• Provide timely updates and information to keep the Board informed of organizational opportunities, challenges, and risks.

• Establish and monitor key performance indicators tied to organizational and LTBID priorities.

• Regularly report progress, outcomes, financial performance, and emerging issues to the Board and appropriate stakeholders.

Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement

• Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders across Little Tokyo to align clean-and-safe initiatives with organizational goals and build community awareness of LTBID.

• Represent LTBID and serve as the primary liaison with the Little Tokyo community, City partners, and other organizations to coordinate business efforts and response plans.

• Develop and maintain relationships with community and City partners, organizations and other governmental agencies to stay informed of evolving community issues and best practices.

Budget and Resource Management

• Oversee the annual budget process, working with program managers and other stakeholders to develop realistic and achievable budgets.

• Monitor performance against budget and provide regular updates and analysis to the Board President and Board of Directors.

• Oversee vendor and contractor performance, ensuring services meet contractual requirements, established standards, and performance expectations.

• Develop and maintain financial forecasting models that support long-term planning and decision-making.

• Ensure effective organizational systems, policies, procedures, and internal controls are in place.

• Identify and manage operational, financial, contractual, and compliance risks.

• Develop and manage LTBID budget and staffing, ensuring cost-effective allocation of resources.

• Evaluate, recommend, and oversee procurement and implementation of office space, equipment, contracts and related administrative issues

Team Leadership

• Recruit, supervise, develop, and evaluate staff, fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing team.

• Establish clear goals, roles, and performance expectations for staff.

• Build a team committed to strengthening community relationships with the Little Tokyo community.

QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

• A Bachelor's degree in Business, Nonprofit Management, or a related field. Significant work experience will be considered.

• At least 7 years of progressive experience managing business/community initiatives.

• Strong understanding of the Little Tokyo community and demonstrated commitment to community service preferred.

• Experience in overseeing medium to large teams on developing and implementing major initiatives that benefit a distinct community/market, with a measurable outcome.

• Experience in managing/coordinating City of Los Angeles BID function or commensurate City/County or public service function.

• Demonstrated emotional intelligence and professionalism, with the ability to communicate thoughtfully, exercise sound judgment, navigate sensitive situations, and build trusting relationships with diverse stakeholders.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Little Tokyo Business Association offers a competitive executive compensation package commensurate with experience with a salary range of $100,000-$135,000 and comprehensive benefits.

Little Tokyo Business Association is an Equal Opportunity Employer. It is our policy to provide equal opportunity to all employees, applicants and program beneficiaries. Little Tokyo Business Association does not discriminate against any person because of race, creed, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, political affiliation or citizenship. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply.

Envision Consulting was retained by Little Tokyo Business Association to conduct the search for the incoming Executive Director of the Little Tokyo BID.

Applicants needing accommodation for any part of the application process may contact Envision Consulting at 626.714.7577 to request and arrange for assistance.

jobs.title: Growth Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT COFRAME

At Coframe, we are building a future where user and agent interfaces can adapt, evolve, and personalize themselves. We are generating revenue, growing rapidly, and trusted by companies you definitely know.



Coframe is a primarily in-person company based in San Francisco, well-capitalized with backing from Khosla Ventures, Nat Friedman, the founder of Android, and others. Our team is small and talent-dense, consisting of competitive programmers, former founders (including our founder who previously co-founded a unicorn), and AI researchers from top institutions who have created some of the most popular open-source code generation projects.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Growth Marketing Lead to help bring Coframe to market as we enter our next stage of growth. You’ll work across launches, campaigns, customer stories, events, partnerships, and whatever else helps the right companies discover and understand what we’re building.

This is a broad, hands-on role for someone who likes making things happen. One week, you might turn a customer result into a campaign; the next, you might coordinate a product launch, improve a landing page, or bring an event from idea to execution. You’ll work closely with our founders, sales team, Growth Strategists, product team, and customers to decide what matters most and get it shipped.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Run launches. Bring product announcements, new capabilities, customer stories, and campaigns to market. Own the plan and execution across messaging, assets, landing pages, distribution, and follow-up.

Turn customer results into stories. Work with customers and internal teams to find compelling examples of Coframe’s impact. Create case studies, content, and campaigns that make our product and its value easy to understand.

Build programs that create demand. Test channels and ideas that put Coframe in front of the right buyers, from targeted campaigns and partnerships to events and organic content. Learn what generates interest and qualified opportunities, then build on it.

Make our website work harder. Improve key pages and conversion paths through better messaging, clearer proof, and thoughtful experiments. Use Coframe’s own product to help us learn and iterate.

Turn opportunities into action. When a partnership, event, customer milestone, or timely industry conversation creates an opening, figure out what we should do and bring the right people together to make it happen.

Get your hands dirty. Draft copy, brief a designer, QA a page, prepare a launch, analyze results, follow up with a partner, or take on something we haven’t done before.

Help us get better at shipping. Build lightweight systems for planning campaigns, managing assets, tracking results, and keeping projects moving as the company grows.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4–10+ years of experience in growth marketing, demand generation, product marketing, or a similarly broad marketing role at a B2B technology company.

 - Deep proficiency with AI and a track record of using it to meaningfully improve the speed, quality, and effectiveness of your marketing.

 - Experience taking marketing projects from idea to launch, with examples of work you personally drove and the results it produced.

 - A generalist who can set direction, coordinate across teams, and execute the work yourself.

 - Strong writing and creative instincts, with the ability to explain a technical product through clear, concrete examples.

 - Excellent organization and follow-through across multiple fast-moving projects.

 - Comfort working closely with sales, product, engineering, customers, and external partners.

Experience marketing to growth, ecommerce, digital, or product teams is a plus. You don’t need to have owned every channel listed above. We care most about your judgment, ownership, ability to learn quickly, and record of getting strong work into the world.




WHY COFRAME

Elite Team: Our founder is a serial entrepreneur who previously co-founded a $2B+ unicorn with Tom Brady and guest lectures AI at Stanford. Our team includes researchers from top institutions who created some of the world's most popular open-source code generation projects.

OpenAI: We’re the only marketing technology company officially partnered with OpenAI. Our engineers and researchers work directly with their team to co-train a model specifically for our use case, which is a differentiator, and a testament to the technical caliber of our team.

Inbound Leads: We’re currently growing at 120% QoQ with a consistent flood of inbound demand. We’re looking for the right saleshumans to capture this demand and market opportunity.

Top VCs: We’re backed by tier-1 investors including Khosla Ventures, Nat Friedman (former GitHub CEO), and Rich Miner (Android co-founder). Joining now means getting a seat on the rocket ship before our Series A: a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to join in the early innings.

Already Crushing It: For our first product, we built proprietary generative AI technology that enables our Agents to autonomously design, code, debug, and deploy A/B tests, Landing Pages, and Personalization experiences. We effectively 10x testing velocity, replacing agencies, legacy tools, and the need to pull in-house designers and engineers for testing. In the last 6 months, we have already driven $221.4M in incremental revenue for our customers like Dropbox, Replit, and Intuit.



“You guys are insane.” - OpenAI team

“Coframe makes you feel like you have a team of 100 people.” - Replit team

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Financial Data, Reporting & Analytics
jobs.description:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.



Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”



Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.



The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.



About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Engineering Manager for the team that owns the financial core of our revenue cycle product. That's three things: the ledger that records every financial event, the reports that billing managers and CFOs close their books on, and the analytics that tell a practice how it's doing.

You'll manage 6 to 8 engineers, from early-career to Senior Staff, own the roadmap with your product partner, and be accountable for financial correctness across the platform. We're partway through rebuilding this surface: moving a decade of report logic onto a drift-free ledger and a modern OLAP layer, while customers keep closing their books on the old one.


What You'll Do

 - Manage and grow a team of 6 to 8 engineers. Hiring, performance, career growth. Build people who can each run a customer escalation, a data migration, or an incident end-to-end without you in the room.

 - Set the roadmap with your product partner. The goal is to get from building whatever report a customer asked for to customers building their own reports and closing their books without us involved.

 - Own financial correctness. For this team, wrong numbers are a worse failure than a slow page. You'll own the systems that catch silent errors: shadow parity harnesses, cross-report tie-out checks, drift monitoring, and correctness SLOs next to the uptime ones.

 - Lead multi-quarter migrations (ledger report migration, OLAP golden views) incrementally, with parity checks at each step, without breaking anyone's close.

 - Own the customer relationship at the top of the stack. Sit with comptrollers, CFOs, and RCM directors at our largest sites during month-end. Turn their definition of "correct" into software, and turn recurring escalations into roadmap.

 - Run cross-team execution with the payments/posting team, data infrastructure, and ops so upstream changes don't quietly break downstream numbers.



What You Have

 - 5+ years managing software engineers, including senior and staff-level ICs. You've grown engineers into leads and staff engineers, and you can name them.

 - You've shipped financial, reporting, or data-intensive systems in production where the numbers had to tie. You know how a report can be technically correct and still wrong to the person reading it.

 - Backend and data fluency. You can review a query plan, push back on a ledger design, and debug a parity failure yourself. Staff engineers will take you seriously because you engage with the substance.

 - You've set direction for a product surface and can say what it should look like in 12 months.

 - You're comfortable across the table from a CFO explaining why a number moved.

 - Operational discipline: on-call, SLOs, and monitoring for correctness as well as availability.

 - You move fast on incomplete information and reset timelines honestly when the work turns out bigger than expected.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Healthcare RCM, billing, practice management, or clearinghouse background. Or fintech experience with ledgers, close automation, or reconciliation (BlackLine, FloQast, Numeric, Stripe, Modern Treasury).

 - OLAP stores (StarRocks, ClickHouse, Druid) run alongside PostgreSQL.

 - Double-entry accounting, append-only ledgers, or audit-trail requirements.

 - Leading a platform re-architecture while keeping the existing system shipping.

 - Shipping LLM features to production. We run an AI report builder that handles thousands of custom reporting requests.



Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com http://commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.

Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

If you thrive in a hands-on, fast-paced environment where your work has a direct, immediate impact on mission success, this is a great opportunity.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Head of Statistical Programming
jobs.description:
About Us

Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.

It is Kardigan’s mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan’s co-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020.

We have a cutting-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late-stage candidates, and an industry-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

At Kardigan, we are motivated by our values which guide how we work, interact, and achieve our goals. Driven by patients and their families, we are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients and prioritizing their needs above all else. We believe in being authentic—leading with truth to bring out the best in others by creating an environment where every person knows they will be fully accepted. With an eagerness to learn, we encourage the highest levels of curiosity and are open to changing our minds. We are committed to winning as a team with urgency, excellence, and intention, and support each other no matter what role we play or where we sit. Lastly, we strive to enable the impossible because patients are counting on us. We are not afraid to take risks to unlock innovation and advance scientific discoveries.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day.

About the Team:

Kardigan's Clinical Data Analytics team is a collaborative and technical partner in advancing our portfolio of investigational cardiovascular therapies. The team is composed of two closely aligned groups, Statistical Programming and Data Science, that turn clinical trial data into submission-ready outputs and actionable insights. Working closely with colleagues across Biostatistics, Clinical Development, and Data Management, the team produces analysis datasets, statistical outputs, dashboards, and exploratory analyses that support high-quality decisions throughout development.

We are building a team that combines technical excellence with a forward-looking, innovation-driven mindset. Team members have the opportunity to modernize how clinical data is programmed, analyzed, and explored, applying tools like automation and AI to strengthen our work. This helps us move with speed and precision while maintaining the highest standards of quality, ethics, and compliance, supporting our mission to bring transformative treatments to people living with cardiovascular disease.

Job Overview

Kardigan is seeking an experienced and forward-looking leader to serve as Head of Statistical Programming. This individual will be accountable for the strategy, organization, quality, and timely delivery of statistical programming across Kardigan’s clinical portfolio. The role will lead and develop the internal programming team, oversee CRO and contractor partnerships, establish scalable programming standards and quality processes, and provide functional leadership for regulatory submissions and health-authority interactions. The Head of Statistical Programming will also shape Kardigan’s programming technology and operating-model roadmap, including the effective use of SAS, R, automation, reusable tools, and a validated statistical computing environment. The successful candidate will combine strong technical expertise with portfolio leadership, operational discipline, vendor-management experience, and the ability to collaborate effectively across Biostatistics, Clinical Data Management, Clinical Development, Regulatory, Quality, and IT.

Functional Leadership and Organization Development

• Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Statistical Programming organization through effective hiring, coaching, mentoring, and succession planning.

• Develop, implement, and maintain SOPs and programming standards to ensure consistency and quality.

• Define and evolve the Statistical Programming operating model, organizational structure, standards, and capabilities to support a growing clinical portfolio.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, technical excellence, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.

Portfolio Delivery and Regulatory Submissions

• Provide strategic and operational leadership for statistical programming activities across clinical development programs, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality analysis datasets, tables, figures, listings, and supporting documentation.

• Lead programming strategy and execution for regulatory submissions, including NDA/BLA filings, integrated summaries, health authority interactions, and responses to regulatory inquiries.

• Oversee the development and delivery of SDTM, ADaM, define.xml, reviewer guides, and other submission components in accordance with regulatory requirements and CDISC standards.

• Monitor portfolio priorities, milestones, resource needs, dependencies, and risks, implementing mitigation plans as appropriate.

• Serve as the senior Statistical Programming representative for regulatory inspections, audits, submission planning, and cross-functional governance activities.

Quality, Compliance, Standards, and Inspection Readiness

• Establish and maintain programming standards, SOPs, validation frameworks, and quality processes that ensure consistency, regulatory compliance, data integrity, traceability, and inspection readiness.

• Ensure appropriate quality control, documentation, change management, and oversight of both internal and outsourced programming activities.

• Partner with Quality and other stakeholders to address audit findings, CAPAs, and quality improvement initiatives.

Vendor, Resource, and Budget Management

• Develop and execute sourcing strategies using internal resources, CROs, contractors, and functional service providers.

• Manage departmental resources, budgets, capacity planning, vendor performance, and governance processes to support business objectives.

Technology and Cross-Functional Leadership

• Establish and maintain a validated, regulatory-compliant statistical computing environment that supports efficient analysis and regulatory submissions.

• Drive the adoption of automation, reproducible programming, code review, standardization, and reusable programming solutions.

• Provide technical leadership for complex programming initiatives and collaborate effectively with Biostatistics, Data Management, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, and other key stakeholders.

• Define and communicate operational metrics, portfolio status, risks, and resource requirements to senior leadership.

About You

Basic Qualifications

• Master's degree or PhD in Statistics, Biostatistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.

• 10+ years of statistical programming experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or clinical research industry.

• Proven experience leading and managing a team of statistical programmers.

• Demonstrated experience leading major regulatory submissions, including NDA/BLA filings and health authority interactions.

• Deep expertise in SAS

• Comprehensive knowledge of CDISC standards (SDTM and ADaM), regulatory submission requirements, define.xml, reviewer guides, and electronic submission packages.

• Strong understanding of the clinical development lifecycle, statistical analysis, study reporting, submission readiness, and regulatory compliance.

• Experience managing vendors, CROs, outsourced deliverables, budgets, and resource planning.

• Experience supporting regulatory inspections, audits, validated computing environments, and data integrity requirements.

• Ability to provide strategic leadership while remaining technically credible and hands-on when needed.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in cardiovascular clinical development is desirable.

• Expertise in R, modern open-source programming practices, and version-control platforms such as Git.

Exact Compensation may vary based on skills, experience and location.

Pay range

$248,000—$323,000 USD

jobs.title: Software Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About Blueprint

Blueprint is a technology solutions firm headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with teams across the United States. We help organizations turn complex challenges into meaningful outcomes by connecting strategy and execution across AI, cloud, data, product development, and emerging technology.

Our culture is built by people who care deeply about doing exceptional work. We set high standards, take ownership, and continually challenge ourselves and one another to be better. We work hard, support each other, and take genuine pride in what we deliver for our clients, partners, and teams.

At Blueprint, you’ll work alongside talented people with different experiences, expertise, and perspectives. You’ll have opportunities to take on meaningful challenges, expand your skills, and see the impact of what you build.

Bring your perspective. Raise the standard. Build what matters.

In This Role

In this role, you’ll work as a hands-on software engineer building and evolving next-generation systems and AI-powered engineering capabilities. You’ll spend the majority of your time developing software, primarily in Python, while working across systems software, Windows development, automation, developer tools, virtualization, AI/LLMs, and cloud infrastructure. You’ll have the opportunity to turn research ideas and experiments into practical engineering solutions, including AI-powered software engineering, agentic systems, automated testing, program analysis, and scalable engineering platforms. This is an environment where adaptability, strong software engineering fundamentals, and the ability to work through ambiguity are important as you explore new technologies and solve complex engineering problems. The position is onsite in the Puget Sound, WA area and involves close collaboration with other engineers and researchers.

Responsibilities

• Design, implement, test, debug, and maintain software across systems, developer platforms, and AI-powered engineering environments.

• Develop software primarily using Python, C/C++, and PowerShell, with opportunities to work with Rust or C#.

• Build and improve software for Windows operating systems, systems infrastructure, virtualization, and cloud environments.

• Develop automation that improves software engineering, testing, debugging, and developer workflows.

• Build tools and services that integrate AI and large language models with source code, engineering data, tests, logs, and system telemetry.

• Explore and develop solutions involving AI-powered software engineering, agentic systems, automated code generation, test generation, debugging, and program analysis.

• Work with Azure, virtual machines, cloud infrastructure, and distributed systems to develop scalable engineering solutions.

• Perform in-depth troubleshooting, unit testing, problem diagnosis, and resolution across new and legacy production systems.

• Collaborate with engineers and researchers to turn research concepts and experimental ideas into practical, scalable software solutions.

• Work across technology boundaries, learn new technologies, and contribute to next-generation engineering platforms.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. 2–4 years of professional software engineering experience. Strong foundation in computer science fundamentals, data structures, algorithms, and software design. Hands-on experience developing software using Python and C/C++. Experience with Windows operating systems development, testing, and debugging. Experience troubleshooting complex software or systems issues and performing effective problem diagnosis and resolution. Experience with unit testing and debugging in new and/or legacy production environments. Experience designing and developing software for large or complex systems. Ability to work effectively in ambiguous environments and translate technical or research concepts into practical engineering solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with PowerShell, Rust, or C#.

• Experience with AI/LLMs, agentic systems, or AI-powered developer tools.

• Experience with automated code generation, test generation, program analysis, or developer productivity tooling.

• Experience integrating software with source code, engineering data, logs, tests, or system telemetry.

• Experience with Azure, virtual machines, cloud infrastructure, or distributed systems.

• Experience with virtualization or systems-level software development.

• Experience building engineering automation or developer tools.

• Experience working in research-oriented or highly exploratory software engineering environments.

Salary Range

At Blueprint, we strive to offer competitive pay that reflects the value of our team members. Compensation for this role is influenced by a variety of factors, including skills, education, responsibilities, experience, and geographic market.

For candidates based in Washington State, the anticipated salary range is $100,000-$110,000 USD annually. Please note that we typically do not hire new employees at the top of the posted range. Actual starting pay will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity. The final salary and job title may vary depending on the selected candidate’s qualifications and could fall outside the stated range.

Location: onsite in Redmond, WA

Benefits

Blueprint believes that healthy, supported employees do their best work. Eligible employees have access to a comprehensive benefits package that may include:

• Medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

• 401(k) retirement plan

• Competitive paid time off

• Parental leave

• Professional growth and development opportunities

Benefits and eligibility may vary based on role, employment status, and location.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Blueprint Technologies, LLC is an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital or familial status, military or veteran status, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicant Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in any part of the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@bpcs.com.

jobs.title: Principal Turbomachinery Engineer
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

Critical to achieving K2's vision is deploying our 20-kW high-power spacecraft platform at scale across MEO, GEO, cis-lunar, and deep space. Realizing that vision means actively controlling the heat generated by the high-power payloads our platform hosts. This requires active thermal control systems such as pumped fluid loops, built from fluid turbomachinery, valves, accumulators, and pressure and temperature instrumentation. Scaling to constellations requires someone who can span the mechanical, fluid, electromechanical, and thermal-fluid domains and collaborate closely with the thermal, avionics, software, and production teams to deliver these systems at rate.

As Principal Turbomachinery Engineer, you will define how K2 designs, analyzes, manufactures, tests, integrates, and deploys precision turbomachinery for integration into active thermal control systems. You will own these unique pieces of turbomachinery from concept through integration and rate production. You will be responsible for mission-critical hardware which goes to space.

Responsibilities

• Responsible for turbomachinery mechanisms in the spacecraft active thermal control system, including:

• Architectural down-selection, design, and tolerancing

• Pump- and mechanism-specific analyses (rotor dynamics, bearings and seals, hydraulic performance, structural, thermal-fluid)

• Environmental test and qualification plans

• Ground- and in-flight performance validation plans

• Supply chain and high-volume manufacturing trades

• Partner with the thermal and platform architecture teams to scope the long-term K2 pumped-fluid-loop roadmap, and system performance requirements

• Collaborate with thermal, structures, avionics, and satellite bus teams to determine optimal operations and requirements for the pump, supporting mechanisms, and broader fluid loop

• Prepare design reviews to secure stakeholder buy-in and communicate expectations across hardware, software, test, and manufacturing teams

• Own and refine program deliverables and schedules throughout development and production

• Evaluate and select manufacturing equipment for specialty processes (impeller machining, rotating-assembly balancing, leak/flow test)

• Partner with production to develop work instructions, in-process checkouts, and end-of-line tests

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or other relevant engineering discipline

• 8+ years of experience with mechanical and/or electromechanical design and analysis

• 2+ years of experience design and analysis of turbomachinery in harsh environments

• Experience with CAD or FEA software packages

Nice to Have

• Experience designing, building, and testing centrifugal or axial pumps for closed-loop thermal systems, including impeller geometry, volute/diffuser design, and hydraulic performance prediction

• Experience with NASA-STD-5017, SMC-S-016, and GSFC-STD-7000 for the design and qualification of in-space Moving Mechanism Assemblies

• Experience with bearing analysis, preload techniques, and preload measurement

• Experience with the practical application of GD&T

• Demonstrated ability to own moving mechanism assemblies across the full product lifecycle in a high velocity environment

• Demonstrated understanding of structural analysis and failure modes of complex mechanical systems in space environments and operations

• Independent and self-motivated mindset, with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills across disciplines

Compensation and Benefits:

• Base salary range for this role is $175,000 - $200,000 + equity in the company

• Salary and level will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level

• Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Export Compliance

As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.”

The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including the export control regulations outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). The person hired for this role must therefore either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.15 or otherwise eligible for a federally issued export control license.

Equal Opportunity

K2 Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with K2 Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Senior Solutions Architect, Partner Business (Channel & Managed Services)
jobs.description:
The Role

You'll build, grow, and scale partner practices across our channel and managed service provider (MSP) network, serving as the technical and product expert across the full partner lifecycle. Instead of focusing solely on individual deals, you will enable entire partner organizations, coaching their technical practitioners and delivery teams to independently deliver solutions on Everlaw's platform.

This is a full-time, exempt position based in our Oakland, CA, New York City, or Washington, D.C. office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.

What you'll do

• Serve as the technical expert across the partner lifecycle, evaluating prospective partners' delivery capabilities and translating complex workflow requirements into platform-native solutions.

• Build onboarding programs, technical playbooks, certification paths, and demonstration enablement materials that accelerate partner ramp-up and independence.

• Deliver polished demonstrations and technical deep dives (including generative AI capabilities and API integration architectures) to technical and executive stakeholders.

• Partner with Business Development and direct sales teams on strategic joint opportunities, RFP responses, and co-sell pursuits.

• Act as an escalation point and technical mentor for partner-side solutions architects, consulting on how Everlaw fits into broader legal technology stacks.

• Gather field insights from partner engagements to collaborate with product and engineering teams on platform features and API surface expansion.

About You

• You have 3+ years of experience in a sales engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting role, with roughly 8+ years of total technology experience and deep hands-on expertise with legal technology platforms.

• You bring a proven track record of working with managed service providers or legal industry delivery teams, with the ability to coach and enable other technical practitioners.

• You have strong technical acumen and a solid command of litigation technology processes, data processing, analytics, and platform integrations.

• You are an excellent communicator and presenter who can influence both delivery engineers and partner executives.

• You are organized and process-oriented, comfortable managing long partnership cycles, concurrent enablement workstreams, and up to 25% travel.

• You are authorized to work in the United States. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring U.S. employment visas for this role.

Think you're missing some of the skills and are hesitant to apply? We do not believe in the 'perfect' candidate and encourage you to apply if you feel you can bring value to our team. We often revisit candidates who may have applied for a different role if something comes up that's a better fit.

The Team: Solutions Architect

The Solutions Architect team brings together product, technical, and ediscovery expertise to show customers how Everlaw can address their most important challenges. Through discovery, tailored demonstrations, technical deep dives, evaluations, and solution design, the team translates complex legal workflows into a clear vision of what better work can look like. This work gives customers confidence in Everlaw while bringing field insights back into the company's product and strategy.

Total Rewards & Benefits

The annual base salary for this position is $172,000, with a total On-Target Earnings (OTE) of $246,000. Eligibility for the commission portion is performance-based and subject to the achievement of specific performance metrics, which are governed by Everlaw's policies and incentive plans. The final offered salary will be dependent upon many factors including the candidate’s experience and skills. The role's compensation is subject to change in the future.

Health & well-being

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Flexible Spending Accounts for health and dependent care expenses

• Membership to Modern Health to support mental health and wellness

• Paid parental leave

• Company-sponsored life and disability insurance

Financial rewards

• Competitive equity grants, so you share in Everlaw's long-term growth

• 401(k) plan with company matching of up to 4% of eligible annual compensation

Growth & everyday perks

• 17 paid vacation days, 11 federal holidays, and paid sick leave

• Four "Everlawlidays" (additional paid company-wide days off) per year

• Annual allocation for learning & development and relevant professional membership dues

• Hybrid work with regular work-from-home days and flexibility for life's logistics

• Monthly home internet reimbursement, plus a stipend for your desk setup

• Catered lunch each workday, plus snacks and company-wide events in our offices

About Everlaw

When a lawsuit or investigation happens, teams must comb through vast amounts of electronic evidence (emails, documents, chats, files) to find what matters. That work is not a side task but the case itself, and where most of the time and money in litigation goes. Everlaw is the litigation and investigation management platform changing that, using AI to turn mountains of messy data into the handful of facts that win or lose a case, compressing weeks of work into hours.

We're the kind of place that's ranked #1 on G2 in our category and named a Great Place to Work™ by our own team. So if you want a front row seat to an industry in transformation, career-defining work you'll be proud to tell people about, and real upside at a company in control of its own destiny, we'd love to get to know you.

• #LI-BL1

• #LI-Hybrid

​​About Everlaw

At Everlaw, you'll shape how AI re-wires the legal industry, at a category-leading business built on a mission to illuminate the truth.

Everlaw is an equal opportunity employer. We pride ourselves on having a diverse workforce and we do not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law. We respect the gender, gender identity and gender expression of our applicants and employees, and we honor requests for pronouns. It is our policy to comply with all applicable national, state and local laws pertaining to nondiscrimination and equal opportunity, including the California Equal Pay Act.  Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

We collect and process the personal information you provided along with your job application in accordance with our Applicants Privacy Notice and Notice at Collection.

When preparing to engage with Everlaw as a candidate, you may use AI tools for research, polishing application materials, and interview prep. However, any assessments (unless explicitly stated), remote interviews or live interviews must be completed independently without AI support. By submitting your application, you agree to adhere to these rules. Here's the link to our full policy, and please reach out with any questions!

jobs.title: RF Validation Associate (Winter 2027)
jobs.description:
Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military.

With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization.

Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA.

RF Validation Associate (Winter 2027)

Associate Engineer positions typically last for twelve weeks, and are salaried roles designed for students who have already received a bachelor's degree (or who will have done so before working at Astranis).

As an Associate Engineer, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on challenging projects, and our Associate Engineers work on projects that are of equal importance and difficulty to the projects we give our full-time employees. Many past Associate Engineers have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many now work at Astranis full-time.

If you are still a college student, please apply to join us as an Intern.

Role

• Measure and validate performance of; LNAs, power amplifiers, up/down converters, filters, oscillators, etc.

• Write automation code to automate and speed up the above measurements

• Document test plans, measurement methodologies, and data for review

Requirements

• Hold a Bachelor's Degree program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, applied physics, or related technical field

• Passion for hardware development, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development

• Deep knowledge of basic RF concepts, such as transmission lines, S-parameters, RF building blocks (amps/mixers/attenuators)

• Experience with Python and object oriented programming concepts

• Experience taking RF measurements with spectrum analyzers, signal generators, network analyzers, etc.

• Don't meet them all? Not a problem. Please apply even if you do not meet all these criteria.

Bonus

• Antennas and Electromagnetics propagation knowledge and background

• Experience with Software Defined Radios (SDR)

• Experience automating RF measurements

The base salary for this position is $1,925 per week.

Base Salary

$1,925—$1,925 USD

U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required

(To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3))

Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. We believe in a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we invite all people to join our team and bring their unique perspectives to make us stronger.

• Opt-Out: You can cancel this service at any time by replying STOP. We will send one final text confirming your unsubscription.

• Opt-In Again: To resume receiving messages, reply START or YES.

• Support & Rates: For assistance, reply HELP or contact us at coordinators@astranis.com. Message and data rates may apply. Message frequency varies; carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.

• Privacy: For details on how we protect your data, view our Privacy Policy.

At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Omnicare is a leading provider of pharmacy services to long-term care facilities nationwide, supporting skilled nursing facilities, assisted living communities, and other institutional care settings. As we transition to an independent, standalone organization, we are building and strengthening internal capabilities to support our approximately 6,000 colleagues and multi-state operations.

Position Summary:

Looking for a career that rewards you? As a Back-End Pharmacy Technician with Omnicare, you will not only find rewarding work in your community, but a team focused on providing a supportive and innovative team environment for all members.

As an Back-End Pharmacy Technician, you will work to ensure all medication needs and regulatory standards are met for our patients. Although Omnicare pharmacies are not open to the public, you’ll work amongst great colleagues in a supportive environment aligned with the company’s mission, allowing our customers to focus on giving their patients the best care.

• Certification/licensed/registered pharmacy technician or as required by state law
• One (1) or more years of experience as a pharmacy technician or equivalent experience

jobs.title: Network Deployment Manager I, Global Network Delivery
jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a fast paced technology company and a leader in the world of data centers. We are currently expanding our network deployment team and are looking for a proven technology manager with experience in people management, robust technical understanding and the drive and vision to take AWS data centers to the next level. The successful candidate for this role will create sustainable processes and standards to reduce delivery cycle times and to improve quality without impacting network availability.

The mission of the team is to deliver network capacity on time with zero rework. The Network Deployment Manager will manage the implementation and delivery of inbound capacity and equipment. This manager will be responsible for a growing a team and will oversee their development and growth. The successful candidate will have experience leading projects, managing and mentoring people, and demonstrate the ability to to collaborate with others to deliver technical solutions. This manager will ultimately be responsible for installing and delivering our network equipment and related infrastructures, as well as responsible for driving low voltage structured cabling across the Amazon data center platform.

Key job responsibilities
-  Managing a team of technicians responsible for installation and deployment of new network systems and projects.
-  Prioritize and assign tasks to data center technicians and operators, project management, coaching and creating documentation.
- Manage inbound capacity from receiving through deployment stages.
- Manage the installation network and cabling infrastructure in a data center environment.
- Guide, train and educate staff on the best practices related to all service owner issues.
- Manage tasks and deliverables across small to large-size projects.
- Recommend, document, and oversee policies and procedures to meet industry best practices and to meet required SLAs.
- Coordinate team resources to support project and delivery needs, to include emergency projects, change management and maintenance window support, and potential off-hours and on-call needs.
- Recruit and train data technicians to ensure appropriate staffing levels.
-  Drive compliance to Amazon performance management requirements.

About the team
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

- Bachelor's degree, or 3+ years of equivalent experience
- 2+ years of Information Technology (IT) experience
- 2+ years of management/team lead function experience

Preferred qualifications:
- Experience with network hardware: copper and optical fiber cabling, switches, routers
- Experience with Lean/Six Sigma
- Knowledge of cabling best practices
